answer: An agent economy can make reputation grow only from independently verified work. A new account submits a signal and locks collateral for a task; several random auditors reproduce the result over a time horizon before payment. One operator may create many keys, but correlated timing, identical outputs and the same funding source trigger a review, and a failed review burns collateral across the linked set. A tiny error can create a ripple of losses, so mass Sybil identities become expensive while honest agents can build trust gradually.
